channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Faces Single International Internet Traffic Operator
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is left with only one operator for international internet traffic. This consolidation raises concerns about the country's digital infrastructure and connectivity.

item.title: Sar-e Pol Declared Second Mine-Free Province in Afghanistan
item.description: Afghanistan's National Disaster Management Authority, now under Taliban control, has declared Sar-e Pol province free of mines and explosive materials. This follows a similar declaration for Bamyan province, marking the end of 36 years of demining operations.

item.title: Afghan Women Face Healthcare Crisis as Hundreds of Clinics Close
item.description: Nearly 300 health facilities in Afghanistan have closed or suspended services this year, impacting over one million women and girls. UN Women reports that funding cuts and Taliban bans on female health workers exacerbate the crisis, leaving many without essential care.

item.title: Uzbekistan Identifies Lack of Information as Key Barrier to Free Healthcare
item.description: Many in Uzbekistan struggle to access free medical care not due to organizational issues, but a lack of awareness about available services and where to seek them. The State Medical Insurance Fund highlights that informing citizens is crucial for improving access.

item.title: OTP Group Acquires Remaining State Shares in Ipoteka Bank, Increasing Stake to 90.4%
item.description: Hungary's OTP Group is acquiring the remaining approximately 17.5% of state shares in Ipoteka Bank. Following the transaction, OTP Group's stake will reach 90.4%. Since joining OTP Group in June 2023, Ipoteka Bank has undergone significant transformation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Greenhouse Owners Seek More Time to Abandon Coal Heating
item.description: Greenhouse owners in Uzbekistan are requesting an extension beyond the December 1st deadline to switch from coal to gas, electricity, or other renewable energy sources. They cite difficulties in meeting strict emission standards for continued coal use and challenges with liquefied gas conversion.

item.title: International Kurash Tournament Held in Termez, Uzbekistan
item.description: An international open Kurash tournament dedicated to the memory of Al-Hakim at-Termizi is underway in Termez. Organized following a presidential decree, the event features over 15 countries and 100 Uzbek athletes competing in three weight categories. The prize fund is $42,000 USD.

item.title: Uzbekistan Unveils Plan for Transition to Revised Latin Alphabet
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Justice has released a draft resolution for public discussion on transitioning all sectors to a revised Latin alphabet. The plan outlines a phased adoption for government bodies, educational institutions, and media, with the new alphabet to take effect April 22, 2027.

item.title: Head of Electronic Technology Development Center Sentenced to 15 Years
item.description: Omоnillokhon Khodjiakbarov, head of Uzbekistan's Center for the Development of Electronic Technologies, has been sentenced to 15 years in prison. A military court found the major general guilty of disclosing state secrets and abusing his official powers.

item.title: Uzbekistan Health Insurance Fund Explains Regional Free Medicine Access Difficulties
item.description: Residents in Uzbekistan's regions face challenges accessing free medicines due to uneven pharmacy network development, despite unified state medical insurance rules. The Health Insurance Fund noted that while Tashkent has the highest availability, the system is uniform nationwide. Addressing the issue requires developing the pharmacy network alongside funding.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Australia Hold Initial Discussions on Sending Citizens for Work
item.description: Uzbekistan and representatives from Australia's Northern Territory have held initial practical discussions regarding the employment of Uzbek citizens. The talks focused on the demand for skilled personnel, particularly in the oil and gas sector, and mechanisms for legally placing Uzbek workers in Australia.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces New Drug Testing for Civil Servants
item.description: Kazakhstan has implemented a new procedure for drug testing civil servants. Officials exhibiting suspicious behavior, such as unexplained absences or mood swings, may be sent for medical examination. Refusal to undergo testing or a positive result can lead to dismissal from service.

item.title: New Epilepsy Treatment Method Successfully Applied in Aktobe
item.description: The first surgery to implant a vagus nerve stimulator (VNS) for epilepsy treatment has been performed in Aktobe, Kazakhstan. The high-tech operation was conducted by specialists at the regional hospital in collaboration with doctors from the National Center for Neurosurgery in Astana. This advanced treatment is now accessible locally.

item.title: Four Kazakh Students Detained in Slovakia on Suspicion of Kidnapping
item.description: Four citizens of Kazakhstan have been detained in Slovakia on suspicion of kidnapping. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed consular and legal assistance is being provided. Reports indicate the students allegedly broke into a home, impersonated special forces, and assaulted a resident while demanding money.

item.title: Uzbekistan Sambo Team Secures First Place at SCO Open Tournament
item.description: The Uzbekistan national sambo team, comprising seven athletes, achieved first place overall at the SCO Open Tournament in Moscow. They secured seven medals, including four gold, one silver, and two bronze, outperforming competitors from ten countries.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Kazhydromet Warns of Air Pollution Risk in Ten Cities
item.description: Kazhydromet has issued a warning for unfavorable meteorological conditions in ten Kazakh cities on Sunday, November 22. These conditions can lead to the accumulation of pollutants near the ground. PM2.5, nitrogen dioxide, and hydrogen sulfide exceedances were previously recorded.

item.title: Uzbekistan's exports grew 33 percent in Jan-Oct 2026, Trend reports
item.description: Uzbekistan's exports, excluding special exports, increased by 33 percent year-on-year to $25.7 billion in January-October 2026, according to Azerbaijani agency Trend. Foreign investment and loans reached $49.5 billion. Uzbekistan aims to join the WTO in 2026.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Hungary discuss cooperation in legal education
item.description: Uzbekistan and Hungary have discussed expanding cooperation in legal education. A delegation visited Hungary to study advanced foreign experience and strengthen ties with international institutions. Discussions included academic exchange and joint educational programs.

item.title: Protection of Child Rights: Key to Society's Prosperous Future
item.description: Protecting children's rights is crucial for society's future, ensuring their potential is realized. Uzbekistan ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1992. While legal frameworks have improved, new challenges like cyberbullying and digital privacy threats emerge. The article discusses the Convention's significance and Uzbekistan's national system for child protection.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Emergency Situations Saved 428 Lives in First 10 Months
item.description: In the first 10 months of the year, Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Emergency Situations (MES) received over 2.79 million appeals from citizens. MES rescuers saved 428 lives, including victims of road accidents, drownings, mountain incidents, and fires. Additionally, first aid was provided to 731 individuals before medical personnel arrived. The ministry also conducted significant work on cleaning water bodies and flood protection.

item.title: Samarkand's "Shirin" District Offers Expanded Benefits for Projects Over $30 Million
item.description: Uzbekistan's "Shirin" district in Samarkand will provide expanded benefits for large urban development projects valued at over $30 million. These incentives, part of a presidential decree, apply to projects meeting criteria for high multiplicative effect and investment, architectural, and tourism appeal. Investors can receive a 20-year exemption from property and land taxes. The benefits cover various building types, including skyscrapers, hotels, and cultural facilities.

item.title: Former Uzbek Official Suspected of Embezzlement Arrested in Turkey
item.description: An Uzbek woman, internationally wanted for embezzlement and document forgery, has been apprehended in Turkey through a joint operation by Uzbek and Turkish law enforcement. She is accused of misappropriating state funds during her tenure at the Employment Assistance Center in the Khorezm region. Investigations are ongoing.

item.title: 1.5 Million Afghanis Missing from Kabul Bank Branch, Investigation Underway
item.description: Hasht-e Subh Daily reports 1.5 million Afghanis are missing from a New Kabul Bank branch. A joint inspection by Kabul Bank and Da Afghanistan Bank found the shortfall. While some experts suggest accounting errors, the possibility of theft and abuse of authority remains. The branch has been ordered to recover the funds.

item.title: Kazakhstan Detains Group Organizing Illegal Border Crossings
item.description: In the Zhambyl region, Kazakhstan detained three citizens and one foreigner suspected of organizing illegal border crossings. A criminal case has been initiated. The operation also uncovered 293 migration law violations, including illegal employment and failure to notify authorities about arriving foreigners. 77 foreign citizens were expelled from Kazakhstan.

item.title: Two Former Commanders Arrested in Connection with Kyrgyz Military Helicopter Crash
item.description: Two former commanders of the Kyrgyz Air Force, including ex-commander Kylychbek Aidaraliev and a unit commander Daniyar Davitahunov, have been arrested. They face charges related to violating flight safety regulations, leading to a fatal Mi-8MTV helicopter crash in January 2024. Both have been detained until December 2026.

item.title: Kazakhstan Updates Rules for Child Registration and School Bullying Prevention
item.description: Kazakhstan has revised its regulations for registering preschool and school-aged children, including those with health exemptions. The updated rules also emphasize bullying prevention, requiring educational bodies to register all reported incidents within one working day and provide psychological support to victims. Schools must also address students with repeated unexcused absences.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank Discusses Financial Sector Development with Commercial Banks
item.description: The Chairman of the National Bank of Kyrgyzstan, Almaz Baketaev, met with commercial bank representatives to discuss the current state and development priorities of the banking sector. The meeting, held on November 20, focused on the activities of financial organizations. Specific decisions were not detailed, but the discussion occurred amid growth in key financial indicators for Kyrgyz commercial banks.

item.title: OTP Bank to Acquire Remaining 17.5% Stake in Ipoteka-Bank from Uzbekistan Government
item.description: Hungarian OTP Bank has agreed to purchase the remaining 17.5% of Ipoteka-Bank shares from the Uzbekistan government. An addendum to the original share purchase agreement was signed, adjusting terms due to significant improvements in Uzbekistan's economic situation since the initial deal in December 2022. The second stage of privatization is expected to conclude soon.

item.title: New Rules for Unexcused Absences and Bullying Take Effect in Kazakhstan Schools
item.description: Kazakhstan has implemented new regulations for tracking students with unexcused absences and preventing bullying. Local education departments must register children aged 18 and under in a unified database, including data on frequent absences. If a child misses four or more days unexcused in a month, the school must consider pedagogical support. Education departments must now register bullying reports within one working day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Airways Takes Delivery of New Airbus A321neo with Enhanced Features
item.description: Uzbekistan Airways has received its sixth Airbus A321neo, featuring a special livery celebrating Uzbekistan's 35th independence anniversary. The new aircraft boasts updated cabins with premium seats, including fully reclining business class seats, and an advanced in-flight entertainment system with screens at every seat. High-speed onboard internet is also available.

item.title: Fire at Iraqi Power Plant Kills Four, Injures 30
item.description: A fire at the Al-Haritha power plant in Basra, southern Iraq, has resulted in at least four deaths and 30 injuries. The blaze caused the plant to cease operations. Civil defense teams have extinguished the fire, which also spread to nearby homes. The cause and extent of damages are under investigation.

item.title: Kazakhstan's President Replaces National Security Committee Chief Amid Corruption Probe
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has replaced the head of the National Security Committee (KNB), Ermek Sagimbayev, with his deputy Marat Irmenov. The move follows a corruption case within the 'Samruk-Kazyna' fund and perceived missteps by security forces. The Minister of Internal Affairs also received a reprimand.

item.title: Former Kyrgyz Air Force Commander Arrested in Military Helicopter Crash Case
item.description: The former commander of Kyrgyzstan's Air Force, Kylychbek Aidaraliev, and a former unit commander, Daniyar Davitahunov, have been detained in connection with a Mi-8 MTV helicopter crash near Bishkek in January 2024. Both face charges of violating flight rules, which resulted in one death and ten injuries.

item.title: Tajik and Russian Presidents Discuss Migration, Security, and Economic Ties in Dushanbe
item.description: Emomali Rahmon and Vladimir Putin met in Dushanbe to discuss migration, regional security, and economic cooperation. Migration, a critical issue for Tajikistan where remittances form a large part of GDP, was a key agenda item. The EU's recent sanctions on Russian bank Unistream, used by Tajik migrants, were also noted.

item.title: Four Kazakh Citizens Detained in Slovakia, MFA Confirms
item.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan has confirmed the detention of four Kazakh citizens in the Slovak Republic. Consular and legal assistance is being provided to the citizens, and contact has been established with their relatives. The situation is under the control of the MFA.

item.title: New US Ambassador to Kyrgyzstan Presents Credentials to Foreign Ministry
item.description: The new US Ambassador to Kyrgyzstan, Stephen Gillen, has presented copies of his credentials to Deputy Foreign Minister Meder Abakirov. During their meeting, both sides discussed the development of bilateral cooperation, with a particular focus on expanding trade and economic ties and promoting joint projects. They affirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in various areas of mutual interest.

item.title: Man Detained in Kyrgyzstan's Alay District Suspected of Wife's Murder
item.description: A man has been detained in the Alay district of Osh region, Kyrgyzstan, on suspicion of murdering his wife. Police report that he allegedly strangled his wife during a drunken argument. A criminal case has been initiated, and the suspect is in custody.

item.title: Afghanistan's UN Missions Mark 80 Years, Call for Preserving Diplomatic Legacy and Rights
item.description: Afghanistan's political missions to the UN marked the 80th anniversary of its membership, stressing the preservation of international commitments and the protection of citizens' rights. They called for an effective UN role in Afghanistan's crisis and urged the safeguarding of women's rights and inclusive governance.

item.title: Kazakhstan MFA Confirms Detention of Four Students in Slovakia
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed the detention of four Kazakh citizens in Slovakia. The students, aged 18-21, are accused of attempting to extort money from a man by posing as police officers. One suspect remains at large.

item.title: First Neurosurgical Implant for Epilepsy Performed in Aktobe
item.description: Doctors in Aktobe successfully implanted a vagus nerve stimulator (VNS) in a 50-year-old epilepsy patient. This high-tech surgery, part of a two-day masterclass, marks a regional first. The VNS technology is used for severe, drug-resistant epilepsy cases to reduce seizure frequency and intensity. The masterclass also included other advanced neurosurgical procedures.
